findings.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the raw zod safeParse result ({success, data}) instead of .data, and Google stores that wrapper directly as credential.key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse() data shape. With the sync feature disabled (default path: schema.safeParse), the first routine Google token refresh persists credential.key = {success: true, data: {...}}; the next GoogleCalendarService instantiation runs googleCredentialSchema.parse on that wrapped key, which fails because access_token is no longer top-level, so every Google Calendar operation 500s for that user until they reconnect — this corrupts credentials on every deployment, not just credential-sharing installs.

[BUG] The sync branch returns the raw, unconsumed global fetch Response while every call site expects a provider-specific parsed object (axios-style .data, Lark envelope, an already-read JSON body), and response.ok is never checked. Whenever APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the parent app's response body is never parsed and no call site can consume it, so token refresh fails for every integrated provider (Google, HubSpot, Lark, Zoom, O365, Webex, Zoho) at the first expired-token operation, making the entire credential-sync feature unusable.

[BUG] In sync mode res is a fetch Response, so res?.data is undefined and token.access_token throws TypeError. With credential sharing enabled, the first Google token refresh after access-token expiry throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading access_token)'; the credential is never updated and every Google Calendar call for that user fails until the feature is disabled or the user reconnects.

[BUG] In sync mode tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and the subsequent tokenInfo.data.error access throws TypeError. With credential sharing enabled, BiginCalendarService's connection setup throws on the first refresh attempt, so every Zoho Bigin calendar operation (event create/update/availability check) fails with a 500.

[BUG] In sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a fetch Response, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined and the following zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error check throws TypeError. With credential sharing enabled, Zoho CRM service construction/refresh throws on the first attempt, so every Zoho CRM calendar operation fails with a 500 for users of that integration.

[BUG] The sync branch's fetch Response is assigned to hubspotRefreshToken (typed HubspotToken), so every token field read from it (.access_token, .expires_in, .refresh_token) is undefined because the Response body is never parsed. With sharing enabled, HubSpot's refreshed-token object is all-undefined, the expiry arithmetic produces NaN, and the credential is updated with garbage — all HubSpot API calls then fail with 401 and the stored credential no longer contains a usable refresh token.

[BUG] The sync Response is passed to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's {code: 0} response envelope, but the documented sync payload (access token + expiry only) contains no code field. With sharing enabled, every Lark token refresh throws the HttpError raised by handleLarkError even when the parent app returned a valid access token, so Lark Calendar operations fail as soon as the stored token expires.

[BUG] Both computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the same literal '[object Object]' (ZodType has no custom toString) and collapse, so minimumTokenResponseSchema degenerates to {access_token: string} — the 'any numeric property is the expiry' intent is not implemented at all. In sync mode every provider schema is bypassed and only access_token survives parsing: Salesforce's persisted credential loses instance_url/id/signature/scope so the next jsforce.Connection hits the wrong endpoint and fails, and O365/Zoom expiry never advances so a sync-endpoint round-trip runs on every single API call; the comment also misleads integrators about the accepted contract.

[BUG] The spread of tokenResponse.data — which is {access_token, refresh_token: 'refresh_token'} whenever the minimum schema is selected — overwrites the user's real refresh_token, and the following prisma.credential.update persists the result. The real Office 365 refresh token is irrecoverably replaced by the literal string 'refresh_token' in the stored credential; once credential sharing is disabled (or the config is partial), every subsequent refresh sends that garbage token and fails, forcing the user to fully reconnect Office 365.

[BUG] Schema selection checks only APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, while refreshOAuthTokens additionally requires a non-null userId, so the two functions disagree on whether sync mode is active. Team-owned credentials (userId null) take the normal provider refresh path but get the real provider response parsed by minimumTokenResponseSchema — the freshly rotated refresh_token is discarded and replaced by the 'refresh_token' placeholder before the value reaches the persisting flows, silently destroying team credentials while the feature is enabled.

[BUG] The outbound sync request sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication — CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is enforced on the inbound webhook but never sent on this fetch, and userId values are small enumerable integers. Anyone who learns CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can POST a userId+appSlug pair and receive that user's live OAuth access token, and the parent application is given no mechanism to verify the caller, so a credential leak is one URL disclosure away.

[ADVISORY] An unconditional token refresh (POST to login.salesforce.com) plus a credential DB write now runs on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, where the previous code built a jsforce.Connection that refreshed lazily only when needed. Every Salesforce calendar operation pays an extra Salesforce round-trip and a DB write, and construction now fails hard (HttpError 400) whenever the token endpoint is slow or unreachable — even when the stored access token was still valid — turning a transient Salesforce token-endpoint outage into a total Salesforce integration outage.

[BUG] The third argument passed to refreshOAuthTokens is credentialId (the credential row's id), not credential.userId, so the sync request sends calcomUserId=<credential id>. With sharing enabled, the parent app resolves the wrong record: it either fails to find the user or returns tokens belonging to a different user (whichever user id numerically equals the credential id), which Zoho Bigin then stores on the original user's credential — a cross-user credential mis-assignment.

[BUG] The sync request sends appSlug 'msteams', but this app's identifier everywhere else in the credential-sync protocol (prisma App.slug, appStoreMetadata key, the appId written by the app-credential webhook) is 'office365video'. A parent application that registered MS Teams credentials under the webhook-validated slug 'office365video' receives sync lookups for an unknown slug 'msteams' and can never resolve them, so every office365video token refresh fails while the feature is enabled.

[BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) throw unhandled ZodError/JSON/decrypt exceptions, and the handler never checks req.method before processing the body. A parent app posting a malformed body (e.g. userId as a string), a payload encrypted with a mismatched key or format, or any GET request receives an opaque 500 with a server stack trace instead of a 4xx, so client errors are treated as server errors and integration debugging is blind.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted JSON is persisted directly as credential.key with no validation against the target app's credential schema — appMetadata's slug/type are used only to locate/create the row, never to validate the payload. A parent app syncing a partial payload (e.g. only access_token for google-calendar) gets a 200 'Credentials created', and the stored credential then fails googleCredentialSchema.parse on next use — the app breaks at runtime even though the sync reported success, and integrators have no published field contract to code against.

[ADVISORY] The stated prerequisites ('must be 32 bytes for AES256', 'openssl rand -base64 24') never specify the actual decryption contract symmetricDecrypt enforces — AES-256-CBC, base64 ciphertext carrying a 16-character IV prefix, and the raw env string used directly as key bytes. An integrator following only this documentation cannot produce a payload the webhook accepts: every app-credential webhook call fails inside symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse and returns a 500, and an integrator who base64-decodes the suggested key (24 raw bytes) crashes the handler with an invalid-key-length error.

[ADVISORY] The removed console.error dropped the zodError details and the raw Microsoft response from refresh-failure logging; failures now surface only as the generic 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' thrown inside parseRefreshTokenResponse. Operators debugging the notoriously flaky Office 365 token refresh lose all diagnostic signal — the Microsoft error payload never reaches the logs — turning every O365 auth outage into an undebuggable generic 500.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse envelope ({success, data, error}), and GoogleCalendarService writes that envelope directly into credential.key in place of the parsed credentials object that googleCredentialSchema.parse previously produced. Within one access-token lifetime of this deploy, every Google-connected user's credential.key becomes {success:true,data:{...}} with access_token/refresh_token no longer at the top level; the next refreshAccessToken reads googleCredentials.refresh_token as undefined, all Google Calendar operations fail, and the original refresh_token is unrecoverable in the DB - each user must reconnect Google. This corrupts in the default (non-sharing) configuration.

[BUG] In credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but all nine call sites immediately consume provider-native token shapes (googlecalendar reads res?.data, zoho-bigin/zohocrm read tokenInfo.data.error, hubspot treats the return as HubspotToken, larkcalendar feeds it to handleLarkError which requires {code,msg,data}), and the diff contains no response adaptation for any provider. With sharing enabled, Google refresh dies on token.access_token of undefined (Response has no .data), Zoho Bigin/CRM throw TypeError reading 'error' of undefined at tokenInfo.data, Hubspot persists undefined/NaN token fields, and Lark's handleLarkError throws on every refresh because the sync endpoint's {access_token,expiry} body has no code field - the sharing mode this PR exists to ship is unusable for every wired provider.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService spreads the parseRefreshTokenResponse result - which in sharing mode contains only access_token plus the helper's injected literal refresh_token:'refresh_token' - over the existing credentials and persists it with prisma.credential.update. One sharing-mode refresh replaces the user's real Microsoft refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token' in the database; the next refresh sends that literal to login.microsoftonline.com, receives invalid_grant, and the Office 365 integration is permanently broken with no error surfaced by this code path.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites data.refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the parsed response lacks the field, which is every sharing-mode response by design because minimumTokenResponseSchema does not declare refresh_token. Sharing-mode callers persist the literal as a real OAuth credential: zoomvideo's parsedToken.data (VideoApiAdapter.ts:103) carries refresh_token:'refresh_token' into the adapter's credential storage, and the next refresh presents that literal to zoom.us, receives an error, and permanently breaks the user's Zoom integration; the same injected literal is what overwrites the real token in Office365.

[BUG] The outbound credential-sync fetch sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header or signature, and the shipped protocol (refreshOAuthTokens, the .env.example docs) defines no way for the parent application to authenticate the caller, even though the inbound webhook leg requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The parent app's token endpoint must be deployed effectively unauthenticated to interoperate with this client, so anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can enumerate calcomUserId values and receive live OAuth access tokens for those users' Google/Microsoft/Zoom accounts.

[BUG] Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the same "[object Object]" string (z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString()), so the second entry overwrites the first and the schema enforces nothing except access_token; because z.object strips unknown keys, the expiry the sync endpoint returns is parsed and then discarded. The 'any property with a number is the expiry' validation the comment promises does not exist: sharing-mode responses with no expiry pass validation, and the expiry field is stripped from the parsed data, so Office365 keeps its already-expired expiry_date and re-refreshes on every calendar operation while Google/Zoom end up with undefined/NaN expiry values.

[BUG] BiginCalendarService passes credentialId (the credential row's database id) as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens, whose wire key is calcomUserId, while every other adapter in this diff passes credential.userId. In sharing mode the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id as calcomUserId, so the parent application looks up the wrong user or none, Zoho Bigin token refresh fails or updates another user's token mapping, and the credential-sync feature silently misattributes Bigin credentials.

[BUG] The handler performs no HTTP method check and calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with no try/catch, so any missing or malformed body throws an unhandled ZodError, and a failed decryption (bad ciphertext or wrong CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY length) throws inside symmetricDecrypt the same way. A GET to /api/webhook/app-credential, or a POST with a missing/misspelled field or undecryptable keys, returns a 500 with a stack trace instead of the 4xx that the handler's other status codes promise, leaving integrators debugging their first webhook against server errors with no schema feedback.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse selects minimumTokenResponseSchema based on the global sharing flags rather than on which endpoint produced the response, so in sharing mode Salesforce's own native login.salesforce.com response is stripped to {access_token} and salesforceTokenSchema becomes dead code for that mode. The persisted Salesforce credential loses instance_url, id, signature, scope and token_type (only refresh_token is re-added at line 97), so subsequent loads read undefined instance_url from credentialKey and the Salesforce integration for sharing-enabled deployments breaks on the next connection setup.

[BUG] The webhook resolves the target credential with findFirst({userId, appId}) using no orderBy and no credential identifier in the request payload, but Cal.com permits multiple credential rows per user and app (each OAuth connect creates a new row via createOAuthAppCredential, and the schema has no unique constraint on userId+appId). For any user with two credentials of the same app, the sync overwrites an arbitrary row - destroying that credential's stored tokens when the parent application meant the other one - and two concurrent webhooks can both pass the findFirst and create duplicate rows; the wire contract has no way to address a specific credential at all.

[BUG] The handler reads the secret header via req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] without lowercasing the configured name, while Node lowercases all incoming header keys and only a .env.example comment guards this. An operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME with any uppercase character gets undefined on every lookup and permanent 403 'Invalid webhook secret' responses even when the correct secret is sent, with nothing in the code normalizing or validating the misconfiguration.

[ADVISORY] The new refresh block performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every construction of SalesforceCalendarService, with no expiry check, before jsforce also performs its own internal refresh through the returned Connection. Every booking operation touching a Salesforce calendar now pays an extra login.salesforce.com round-trip and a credential-row DB write per operation, doubling refresh traffic and adding a remote dependency to a hot path that previously refreshed lazily only on auth failure.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a new authenticated webhook endpoint, two behavior-bearing OAuth helpers, and rewires the token-refresh path of nine providers, yet contains no test files at all - no spec/, test/, __tests__/, *.test.* or *.spec.* path appears anywhere in the diff. Nothing verifies parseRefreshTokenResponse's return shape, refreshOAuthTokens' routing, or the webhook's auth/decrypt/upsert behavior; the exact defect this diff ships (Google persisting the safeParse envelope as the credential key) would have been caught by a one-line assertion on the helper's return, so every regression in this untested sharing path reaches production unverified.

[ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse has an ambiguous contract - it throws on failure yet returns the full safeParse envelope and mutates data.refresh_token - and the three in-diff callers interpret it three different ways: Google uses the return value directly as the stored key, Office365 spreads .data, and Salesforce's `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check at CalendarService.ts:91-93 is dead code because the helper already threw. The next contributor copying the Salesforce or Office365 pattern into another adapter - or 'fixing' the helper to return data - silently changes what every other caller persists; the divergent interpretations are already visible in this diff and the store-the-envelope bug is the realized instance.

[ADVISORY] The 'credential sharing active' condition is assembled from three env vars with different subsets in four places: constants.ts:103-104 pairs CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY into APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse each additionally && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, and the webhook gates on the flag alone - with no logging on any fallback branch. An operator who sets the secret and key but omits CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT gets a live inbound webhook silently paired with native local refresh: cal.com refreshes tokens itself and never propagates them, and for refresh-token-rotating providers the parent application's stored tokens are silently invalidated; nothing in the logs distinguishes this half-enabled state from a working sync.

[ADVISORY] The new Salesforce refresh path never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, making Salesforce the one OAuth provider this diff touches whose token refresh is excluded from the credential-sync feature. Self-hosters running credential sharing get Salesforce refreshed locally against login.salesforce.com with cal.com's own app keys; refreshed tokens never reach the parent application, so the parent's Salesforce credential set diverges and the feature's single-owner premise silently fails for this provider.

[BUG] The webhook secret is compared with a plain !== string comparison instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual. The comparison short-circuits on the first differing byte, giving a network-adjacent attacker a timing oracle to recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte-by-byte and then forge credential-overwrite webhooks for any user id.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted keys payload is JSON.parse'd and written straight into credential.key with no schema validation against the target app's credential schema. A parent application that encrypts a malformed payload (wrong field names, or a JSON string instead of an object) overwrites a working user credential with garbage and receives 200 'Credentials updated', leaving the user's integration broken with no error anywhere to diagnose.

[ADVISORY] The sync-endpoint fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, and no error handling, and it sits on the token-refresh path of every calendar and video operation. A hung or slow CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT blocks each affected booking for up to the runtime's multi-minute default header timeout before throwing, turning the self-hoster's own endpoint into a stall point for all bookings that use synced credentials.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) rather than parsed data, and GoogleCalendarService persists that envelope directly as the credential key (data: { key }) instead of the parsed credential the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse() produced. On each user's first token refresh (within ~1 hour of deploy) credential.key becomes {success:true, data:{...}}, so the next load reads refresh_token/access_token as undefined, myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(undefined) throws, and all Google Calendar availability checks and bookings fail for every Google-connected user until each one manually re-authenticates — with the sync feature disabled as well as enabled; the stored credential is corrupted (data loss).

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but this code reads res?.data and then token.access_token, and a fetch Response has no data property. With credential sync enabled, every Google token refresh throws TypeError (reading 'access_token' of undefined) before the parent app's tokens are ever read, so Google Calendar — the primary calendar — fails outright for sync-enabled self-hosters, the exact audience this PR targets.

[BUG] The sync-mode raw fetch Response is assigned to hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken and its body is never parsed (no res.json() anywhere), while the following code reads expires_in/refresh_token off it to compute the expiry and persist the credential. With sync enabled the parent app's access token is discarded entirely, the expiry computes to Date.now() + undefined*1000 = NaN, and a garbage token object is written into the user's HubSpot credential, breaking HubSpot for sync-enabled deployments and forcing re-auth.

[BUG] In sync mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but the code immediately evaluates tokenInfo.data.error at line 96, and a Response has no data property. With sync enabled, every Zoho Bigin token refresh fails with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)', so Bigin calendar operations break for sync-enabled self-hosters — the new shared helper was wired into a caller whose axios-shaped contract it does not satisfy.

[BUG] In sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but the code evaluates zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error at line 217. With sync enabled, every Zoho CRM token refresh throws TypeError reading 'error' of undefined, so Zoho CRM-backed bookings fail for sync-enabled deployments; the refreshOAuthTokens return contract was never normalized for axios-based callers.

[BUG] In sync mode resp is the parent app's response whose documented contract is {access_token, expiry}, but line 82 passes it to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's {code: 0, msg, data} envelope and treats any other body as an error. With sync enabled, every Lark token refresh is rejected by handleLarkError (code is undefined), so Lark Calendar fails for sync-enabled self-hosters even when the parent app returned valid tokens per the contract the PR itself documents.

[BUG] zoho-bigin passes credentialId (the credential row's identifier) as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, which posts it as calcomUserId, while every other adapter in this diff passes credential.userId. In sync mode the parent app receives the credential's database primary key as calcomUserId, resolves the wrong or a nonexistent user, and returns tokens for the wrong account, so Zoho Bigin sync can never work even after the Response-shape breakage is fixed.

[BUG] The outbound request to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication — no copy of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET or any header — even though this same PR authenticates the inbound webhook with a shared secret. The parent app cannot distinguish Cal.com from any network-reachable caller, so an attacker who can reach the endpoint POSTs a userId and receives that user's freshly refreshed OAuth tokens — full credential exfiltration — and the PR provides no credential the parent app could check to prevent it, so the sync protocol's security invariant holds in only one direction.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys evaluate to '[object Object]' (z.string().toString() is Object.prototype.toString), so in sync mode only access_token is ever validated, and the function then overwrites the real refresh token with the literal string 'refresh_token' whenever the parent response omits it. For office365 (…o365AuthCredentials, …tokenResponse.data) and zoom in sync mode, the placeholder spreads over the user's real refresh token and is persisted to the DB, destroying the stored credential — if the self-hoster later unsets CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT the local refresh path sends the literal string 'refresh_token' and fails with invalid_grant until every user reconnects; the expiry validation the comment promises never exists, and the global-env inference also misroutes Salesforce's locally-fetched response into this lenient schema.

[BUG] The SalesforceCalendarService now performs an eager, unconditional fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update on every service instantiation — ungated by APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and not routed through refreshOAuthTokens — where construction previously made no network call or DB write. Every availability check and booking that instantiates the Salesforce service now pays a synchronous Salesforce token refresh and a DB write (hot-path regression affecting all Salesforce users even with the sync feature off), Salesforce is silently exempted from the credential-sync contract the PR implements, and in sync-enabled deployments its locally-fetched response is validated by the lenient minimumTokenResponseSchema instead of salesforceTokenSchema — an ungated behavior change not traceable to the credential-sync requirement.

[ADVISORY] The webhook decrypts keys and JSON.parses the result straight into prisma.credential.update/create without validating it against the app's per-app zod credential schema, even though every other credential write path in this PR parses keys with a schema. A parent app pushing a partial payload — e.g. the {access_token, expiry} shape this PR's own sync contract documents — receives 200 'Credentials updated', and the user's app fails at the next booking with undefined-field errors that neither side can trace back to the sync write; a trusted-but-buggy producer is precisely what the invariant this endpoint skips exists to catch.

[ADVISORY] The webhook lets ZodError from appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse and SyntaxError from JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) escape unhandled. A parent app with a mismatched CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY — the primary operational failure mode of this feature, which the .env.example itself warns must match on both sides — or a malformed body receives a raw 500 instead of a 4xx, so operators diagnose a Cal.com server bug rather than a configuration mismatch and the endpoint's error contract is undefined.

[ADVISORY] The redirectUri hardcodes 'zoho-bigin' in the callback path where the code previously used appConfig.slug — an unexplained change unrelated to the PR's credential-sync requirement. The redirect URI silently diverges from config.json if the slug ever changes, and an undocumented behavioral edit buried inside a 20-file sync PR means anyone bisecting a zoho-bigin OAuth regression is led into this unrelated diff with no requirement or commit message accounting for it.

[ADVISORY] The PR bundles a mechanical ~20-file directory rename (moving the _utils OAuth helpers into _utils/oauth and rewriting every import site) into the same change as behavioral edits to eight adapters' token refresh. The real behavioral regressions in this diff (the Google envelope persistence, the Salesforce eager refresh, the sync Response-contract breaks) are hidden inside no-op-looking import churn, so reviewing and bisecting the credential-sync behavior requires clearing unrelated files first — the mechanical move was separable and should not share a diff with behavior changes.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds three behavior-bearing modules — the webhook handler, refreshOAuthTokens, and parseRefreshTokenResponse — and rewires token refresh in eight adapters with no test anywhere in the diff. Nothing asserts parseRefreshTokenResponse's return contract (envelope vs parsed data), which is exactly the confusion that produced the Google credential-corruption bug in this same diff, so the next contributor touching the now-shared refresh path has no safety net on any of the newly shared code.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full zod safeParse envelope, and this code stores that envelope directly as credential.key, so the persisted google credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the parsed token object. In the default (non-sync) configuration the first token refresh rewrites every google-calendar user's credential into the envelope shape; the next operation reads credential.key.refresh_token as undefined and google auth fails, so all google integrations break within one access-token lifetime (~1 hour) of this deploy and every user must reinstall the app.

[BUG] The sync branch returns a raw fetch Response while every call site was written around the provider-native shape (google's GaxiosResponse with .data, hubspot's token object, zoho-bigin's axios response with .data, lark's lark envelope), and the any return type hides the mismatch from the compiler. With sync enabled every integrating app's refresh is broken: google dereferences undefined res.data and throws, hubspot persists a Response as the credential key, zoho-bigin throws on tokenInfo.data.error, and lark's handleLarkError rejects the non-lark payload — the credential-sync feature ships with no working consumer.

[BUG] The sync branch's fetch Response is assigned to HubspotToken and flows into hubspot's existing code, which computes expiry from .expires_in (undefined on a Response) and persists the object as credential.key. A Response instance has no enumerable own token properties, so JSON serialization stores only {"expiry_date":null} — one sync-mode refresh destroys the stored hubspot access and refresh tokens entirely and the user must re-authenticate.

[BUG] This call passes credentialId (the credential row id) where refreshOAuthTokens' contract requires the user id — every sibling call site in this diff passes credential.userId. The sync request sends calcomUserId=<credential id>, so the parent resolves a different user's tokens on numeric-id collision or none at all, and the returned tokens get persisted into this credential — cross-user credential contamination or guaranteed refresh failure under sync.

[BUG] Both computed keys of minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the same string (z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString() both yield '[object Object]'), so the second declaration overwrites the first and the schema enforces nothing but access_token — the commented 'any property with a number is the expiry' contract is unimplemented. In sync mode zod's default strip behavior reduces every token response to {access_token}: office365calendar keeps its stale expiry_date and re-refreshes on every operation, office365video and zoom derive NaN/undefined expiry from fields that never survive the parse, and no consumer can ever store a usable expiry from the sync endpoint.

[BUG] When the parsed response lacks refresh_token, this code writes the literal string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data as a fake token. The placeholder flows into the stored credential at the office365calendar and zoomvideo call sites, replacing the real refresh token (which the parent's refresh already rotated) with the literal string 'refresh_token', so any later non-sync refresh fails with invalid_grant and the user must re-authenticate.

[BUG] In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse returns only {access_token, refresh_token:'refresh_token'}, which the immediately following existing spread writes over o365AuthCredentials, overwriting the real Microsoft refresh token with the literal placeholder. After one sync-mode refresh the stored office365 credential carries the fake refresh token while Microsoft has already rotated the real one during the parent's refresh, so the credential can never refresh locally again and fails with invalid_grant the moment sync is disabled or the endpoint fails.

[BUG] In sync mode parseRefreshTokenResponse returns {access_token, refresh_token:'refresh_token'} instead of zoomRefreshedTokenSchema's parsed shape, which zoom's existing key merge spreads over the stored credential. The zoom credential's refresh_token is replaced by the literal placeholder while the real one was single-use and already consumed by the parent's refresh, so zoom credentials can never refresh locally and the stored key no longer matches the schema zoom validates against.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so res.data is undefined and token.access_token throws a TypeError (or the surrounding catch swallows it) before the credential is ever updated. Google calendar refresh never succeeds under credential sync, so every google operation after access-token expiry runs with a stale token and fails — google calendar is nonfunctional for sync-enabled self-hosters.

[BUG] In sync mode tokenInfo is a fetch Response, so tokenInfo.data is undefined and the existing tokenInfo.data.error check throws a TypeError. Every zoho-bigin refresh under credential sync crashes before reading the token, so zoho-bigin operations fail once the access token expires.

[BUG] In sync mode resp is a fetch Response from the credential-sync endpoint, but the following handleLarkError expects lark's {code:0,...} envelope and throws for any payload lacking code 0. Every lark refresh under credential sync throws a lark auth error, so lark calendar operations fail once the access token expires.

[BUG] The appSlug sent to the sync endpoint is 'msteams', but this app's slug in the App table and appStoreMetadata is 'office365video' — every other call site in the diff passes its app's real slug. With sharing enabled, Google refresh dies on token.access_token of undefined (Response has no .data), Zoho Bigin/CRM throw TypeError reading 'error' of undefined at tokenInfo.data, Hubspot persists undefined/NaN token fields, and Lark's handleLarkError throws on every refresh because the sync endpoint's {access_token,expiry} body has no code field - the sharing mode this PR exists to ship is unusable for every wired provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, returns a raw `fetch(...)` Response (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Multiple updated call sites still treat the return value as provider-native/axios/gaxios shapes (e.g., Google reads `res?.data` in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts; Hubspot assigns it to `HubspotToken`; Zoho Bigin/CRM expect `tokenInfo.data`; Lark passes it to `handleLarkError`). A WHATWG `Response` has no `.data`, so these paths will break under the credential-sharing mode introduced by this PR, and no adapter/parsing layer was added in the diff to reconcile the types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365CalendarService spreads the parseRefreshTokenResponse result - which in sharing mode contains only access_token plus the helper's injected literal refresh_token:'refresh_token' - over the existing credentials and persists it with prisma.credential.update. One sharing-mode refresh replaces the user's real Microsoft refresh_token with the literal string 'refresh_token' in the database; the next refresh sends that literal to login.microsoftonline.com, receives invalid_grant, and the Office 365 integration is permanently broken with no error surfaced by this code path.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites data.refresh_token with the literal string "refresh_token" whenever the parsed response lacks the field, which is every sharing-mode response by design because minimumTokenResponseSchema does not declare refresh_token. Sharing-mode callers persist the literal as a real OAuth credential: zoomvideo's parsedToken.data (VideoApiAdapter.ts:103) carries refresh_token:'refresh_token' into the adapter's credential storage, and the next refresh presents that literal to zoom.us, receives an error, and permanently breaks the user's Zoom integration; the same injected literal is what overwrites the real token in Office365.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core bug: parseRefreshTokenResponse assigns the literal string "refresh_token" when the field is missing from the OAuth refresh token response, leading to an invalid refresh token being stored and used in subsequent refresh attempts, causing authentication failures/integration breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The outbound credential-sync fetch sends only calcomUserId and appSlug with no authentication header or signature, and the shipped protocol (refreshOAuthTokens, the .env.example docs) defines no way for the parent application to authenticate the caller, even though the inbound webhook leg requires CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The parent app's token endpoint must be deployed effectively unauthenticated to interoperate with this client, so anyone who can reach CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT can enumerate calcomUserId values and receive live OAuth access tokens for those users' Google/Microsoft/Zoom accounts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and no auth header/signature/secret (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). The accompanying `.env.example` additions define `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` but no outbound authentication mechanism, while the inbound webhook path does require `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/header. As implemented, the protocol provides no application-layer way for the parent endpoint to authenticate Cal.com, creating a real security exposure if the endpoint is reachable and returns user access tokens based on those parameters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Both computed keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema evaluate to the same "[object Object]" string (z.string().toString() and z.string().optional().toString()), so the second entry overwrites the first and the schema enforces nothing except access_token; because z.object strips unknown keys, the expiry the sync endpoint returns is parsed and then discarded. The 'any property with a number is the expiry' validation the comment promises does not exist: sharing-mode responses with no expiry pass validation, and the expiry field is stripped from the parsed data, so Office365 keeps its already-expired expiry_date and re-refreshes on every calendar operation while Google/Zoom end up with undefined/NaN expiry values.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property names are evaluated immediately to ordinary string keys (not an index signature), so they do not implement “any property with a number is the expiry”. At best, you end up with one or two fixed keys (very likely the same string, meaning one overwrites the other), and all real token fields like `expiry_date` are treated as unknown. Since `z.object(...)` strips unknown keys by default (no `.passthrough()` here), an expiry field returned by the sync endpoint would be discarded from `.data`. This makes sharing-mode validation far weaker than the comment promises and can prevent expiry updates from being persisted/propagated (e.g., Office365 uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then spreads `tokenResponse.data` into credentials).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BiginCalendarService passes credentialId (the credential row's database id) as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens, whose wire key is calcomUserId, while every other adapter in this diff passes credential.userId. In sharing mode the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id as calcomUserId, so the parent application looks up the wrong user or none, Zoho Bigin token refresh fails or updates another user's token mapping, and the credential-sync feature silently misattributes Bigin credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call was changed to `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)`, whereas `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third argument is clearly a *userId* (`(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)`), and it serializes it as `calcomUserId` in the request body. Every other integration updated in this diff passes `credential.userId` (e.g., Zoom, O365, Webex, Hubspot, etc.). Passing a variable named `credentialId` here is very likely passing the credential row id instead of the Cal.com user id, which would cause the sync endpoint to receive the wrong `calcomUserId` when sharing mode is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler performs no HTTP method check and calls appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) with no try/catch, so any missing or malformed body throws an unhandled ZodError, and a failed decryption (bad ciphertext or wrong CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY length) throws inside symmetricDecrypt the same way. A GET to /api/webhook/app-credential, or a POST with a missing/misspelled field or undecryptable keys, returns a 500 with a stack trace instead of the 4xx that the handler's other status codes promise, leaving integrators debugging their first webhook against server errors with no schema feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler, there is no `req.method` guard (so GET/other methods will proceed) and it uses `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` without any try/catch. `zod.parse` throws on invalid/missing fields, and `symmetricDecrypt(...)` plus `JSON.parse(...)` can also throw on bad ciphertext or missing/wrong `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (it even falls back to `""`). These thrown errors are not converted into controlled 4xx responses, so the route can return an unhandled 500 instead of the explicit 403/404/200 paths shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse selects minimumTokenResponseSchema based on the global sharing flags rather than on which endpoint produced the response, so in sharing mode Salesforce's own native login.salesforce.com response is stripped to {access_token} and salesforceTokenSchema becomes dead code for that mode. The persisted Salesforce credential loses instance_url, id, signature, scope and token_type (only refresh_token is re-added at line 97), so subsequent loads read undefined instance_url from credentialKey and the Salesforce integration for sharing-enabled deployments breaks on the next connection setup.

adjudication.rationale: In `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, the schema choice is gated by global flags: if `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` it uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` regardless of which endpoint actually produced the token response. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh is still performed against Salesforce (`https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token`) and then parsed via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)`. Under sharing+sync-endpoint mode, that call will parse with the minimum schema, which (as a Zod object without passthrough) will not preserve Salesforce-specific fields like `instance_url`, `id`, `signature`, `scope`, `token_type`. The subsequent prisma update persists only the parsed fields plus a re-added `refresh_token`, dropping the rest, which can break later Salesforce usage that relies on those fields being present in the stored credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook resolves the target credential with findFirst({userId, appId}) using no orderBy and no credential identifier in the request payload, but Cal.com permits multiple credential rows per user and app (each OAuth connect creates a new row via createOAuthAppCredential, and the schema has no unique constraint on userId+appId). For any user with two credentials of the same app, the sync overwrites an arbitrary row - destroying that credential's stored tokens when the parent application meant the other one - and two concurrent webhooks can both pass the findFirst and create duplicate rows; the wire contract has no way to address a specific credential at all.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the target credential is located via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` with no `orderBy` and no credential identifier in the request body. The handler then updates that single found row, otherwise it creates a new row. From this diff alone, there is no uniqueness enforcement shown for `(userId, appId)`, and the code itself comments it "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id of the credential", implying multiple rows may exist. In that situation, `findFirst` can select an arbitrary matching credential and overwrite its `key` (token set) incorrectly, and concurrent requests can both miss and then `create`, producing duplicate credential rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler reads the secret header via req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] without lowercasing the configured name, while Node lowercases all incoming header keys and only a .env.example comment guards this. An operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME with any uppercase character gets undefined on every lookup and permanent 403 'Invalid webhook secret' responses even when the correct secret is sent, with nothing in the code normalizing or validating the misconfiguration.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check indexes headers with `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. Node/Next normalizes incoming header names to lowercase keys on `req.headers`, so if an operator sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` with any uppercase characters, this lookup can return `undefined` and the handler will always 403 with "Invalid webhook secret" even when the correct header is sent. The diff only documents "Should be in lowercase" in `.env.example` but does not normalize/validate in code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new refresh block performs an unconditional Salesforce token refresh plus a prisma.credential.update on every construction of SalesforceCalendarService, with no expiry check, before jsforce also performs its own internal refresh through the returned Connection. Every booking operation touching a Salesforce calendar now pays an extra login.salesforce.com round-trip and a credential-row DB write per operation, doubling refresh traffic and adding a remote dependency to a hot path that previously refreshed lazily only on auth failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new logic unconditionally calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)` (no expiry/need check shown). This does add a network round-trip and DB write on the path that constructs/initializes the service/connection, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff. The parts of the finding about jsforce "also" refreshing internally and about prior behavior refreshing only on auth failure are not verifiable from the diff, but the added unconditional refresh+write is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff adds a new authenticated webhook endpoint, two behavior-bearing OAuth helpers, and rewires the token-refresh path of nine providers, yet contains no test files at all - no spec/, test/, __tests__/, *.test.* or *.spec.* path appears anywhere in the diff. Nothing verifies parseRefreshTokenResponse's return shape, refreshOAuthTokens' routing, or the webhook's auth/decrypt/upsert behavior; the exact defect this diff ships (Google persisting the safeParse envelope as the credential key) would have been caught by a one-line assertion on the helper's return, so every regression in this untested sharing path reaches production unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s concrete defect is verifiable in the diff: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result object (e.g., `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed `data` itself (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, which returns `refreshTokenResponse`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would store the safeParse envelope instead of the credential payload. Previously it used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returns the payload. This is a real correctness/data-shape regression that could break downstream code reading `credential.key`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse has an ambiguous contract - it throws on failure yet returns the full safeParse envelope and mutates data.refresh_token - and the three in-diff callers interpret it three different ways: Google uses the return value directly as the stored key, Office365 spreads .data, and Salesforce's `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check at CalendarService.ts:91-93 is dead code because the helper already threw. The next contributor copying the Salesforce or Office365 pattern into another adapter - or 'fixing' the helper to return data - silently changes what every other caller persists; the divergent interpretations are already visible in this diff and the store-the-envelope bug is the realized instance.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper returns the full `safeParse` envelope (with `.success`/`.data`) and throws on failure, so callers should not expect a failing return. The diff shows inconsistent usage: Google Calendar now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists `key` directly to Prisma (`data: { key }`), which will store the *envelope* instead of the credential object (previously it stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` data). Office365 spreads `.data` and Salesforce checks `!accessTokenParsed.success` even though that branch is unreachable because the helper already throws. This inconsistency is visible in the diff and the Google persistence change is a concrete, verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'credential sharing active' condition is assembled from three env vars with different subsets in four places: constants.ts:103-104 pairs CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY into APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse each additionally && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, and the webhook gates on the flag alone - with no logging on any fallback branch. An operator who sets the secret and key but omits CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT gets a live inbound webhook silently paired with native local refresh: cal.com refreshes tokens itself and never propagates them, and for refresh-token-rotating providers the parent application's stored tokens are silently invalidated; nothing in the logs distinguishes this half-enabled state from a working sync.

adjudication.rationale: The diff creates a real “half-enabled” configuration state. `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is truthy when only `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are set (`packages/lib/constants.ts`), and the inbound webhook endpoint gates only on that flag plus secret match (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`). However, the outbound/refresh syncing behavior additionally requires `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`). If an operator sets secret+encryption key but omits the endpoint, Cal.com will accept and store inbound credentials (webhook live) but token refreshes will fall back to native provider refresh (the `else` branch), updating only Cal.com’s stored credentials without propagating updates. For providers that rotate refresh tokens, this can desynchronize/invalidates the parent app’s stored refresh token without any logging to indicate the fallback/misconfiguration (no logs in the fallback branches).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new Salesforce refresh path never routes through refreshOAuthTokens, making Salesforce the one OAuth provider this diff touches whose token refresh is excluded from the credential-sync feature. Self-hosters running credential sharing get Salesforce refreshed locally against login.salesforce.com with cal.com's own app keys; refreshed tokens never reach the parent application, so the parent's Salesforce credential set diverges and the feature's single-owner premise silently fails for this provider.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, most OAuth providers’ refresh flows are routed through the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper (e.g., Google, O365, Zoom, Webex, etc.) to support `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true. However, `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` adds a refresh-token `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly and does not use `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce is indeed excluded from that credential-sync refresh routing. This is a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency/feature gap, but it doesn’t prove a correctness break in Cal.com itself—rather, it suggests the credential-sync feature is incomplete for Salesforce in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook secret is compared with a plain !== string comparison instead of crypto.timingSafeEqual. The comparison short-circuits on the first differing byte, giving a network-adjacent attacker a timing oracle to recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET byte-by-byte and then forge credential-overwrite webhooks for any user id.

adjudication.rationale:
The new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) authenticates requests via a direct string inequality check:
```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```
This is not a constant-time comparison and (as the finding notes) can create a timing side-channel for guessing `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, after which an attacker could send forged credential overwrite webhooks (the endpoint updates/creates credentials for arbitrary `userId` from the request body). Using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (with proper buffer normalization and length check) would mitigate this class of issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The decrypted keys payload is JSON.parse'd and written straight into credential.key with no schema validation against the target app's credential schema. A parent application that encrypts a malformed payload (wrong field names, or a JSON string instead of an object) overwrites a working user credential with garbage and receives 200 'Credentials updated', leaving the user's integration broken with no error anywhere to diagnose.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(...)`d and then written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys }})` / `create({ data: { key: keys, ... }})` with no validation that `keys` matches the expected credential schema for the target app. The only checks performed are for `userId`, `appSlug`, and that `keys` is a string pre-decryption (`z.string()`), plus app existence via `appStoreMetadata`. This means a malformed but decryptable JSON payload can overwrite an existing working credential with invalid structure while still returning HTTP 200 ('Credentials updated/created'), matching the finding's concern about silently breaking integrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sync-endpoint fetch has no timeout, no response.ok check, and no error handling, and it sits on the token-refresh path of every calendar and video operation. A hung or slow CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT blocks each affected booking for up to the runtime's multi-minute default header timeout before throwing, turning the self-hoster's own endpoint into a stall point for all bookings that use synced credentials.

adjudication.rationale: The new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) calls `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` with no timeout/AbortController, no `response.ok`/status handling, and no try/catch. This function is now used in multiple token refresh paths (e.g., GoogleCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, Zoom VideoApiAdapter, Webex, Lark, Hubspot, Zoho, etc.). If the configured sync endpoint is slow/hung, the request will block until the runtime/serverless execution times out, stalling the calendar/video operation that needed a refresh. The diff shows no safeguards against that stall point.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) rather than parsed data, and GoogleCalendarService persists that envelope directly as the credential key (data: { key }) instead of the parsed credential the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse() produced. On each user's first token refresh (within ~1 hour of deploy) credential.key becomes {success:true, data:{...}}, so the next load reads refresh_token/access_token as undefined, myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(undefined) throws, and all Google Calendar availability checks and bookings fail for every Google-connected user until each one manually re-authenticates — with the sync feature disabled as well as enabled; the stored credential is corrupted (data loss).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function returns the Zod `safeParse` result envelope (`{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential object. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, this return value is assigned to `key` and persisted directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. Previously this code used `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` which returns the parsed object itself. Storing the envelope would change the persisted credential shape (e.g., `refresh_token` would be under `key.data.refresh_token`), likely breaking later reads that expect `credential.key.refresh_token` / `credential.key.access_token`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response from CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but this code reads res?.data and then token.access_token, and a fetch Response has no data property. With credential sync enabled, every Google token refresh throws TypeError (reading 'access_token' of undefined) before the parent app's tokens are ever read, so Google Calendar — the primary calendar — fails outright for sync-enabled self-hosters, the exact audience this PR targets.
matched_golden_ids: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response lacking a .data property, so accessing res?.data leads to undefined and token.access_token throws at runtime due to inconsistent return shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync-mode raw fetch Response is assigned to hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken and its body is never parsed (no res.json() anywhere), while the following code reads expires_in/refresh_token off it to compute the expiry and persist the credential. With sync enabled the parent app's access token is discarded entirely, the expiry computes to Date.now() + undefined*1000 = NaN, and a garbage token object is written into the user's HubSpot credential, breaking HubSpot for sync-enabled deployments and forcing re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when sync is enabled (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), the helper performs a raw `fetch(...)` and **returns the Fetch `Response` object** directly (no `await response.json()`). In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result of `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` is assigned to `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = ...`. With sync enabled, that value will be a `Response`, not a `HubspotToken`, so any subsequent reads like `hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in` / `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` will be `undefined` (or throw), leading to bad expiry computation and incorrect credential persistence. This is a concrete type/behavior mismatch introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode tokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but the code immediately evaluates tokenInfo.data.error at line 96, and a Response has no data property. With sync enabled, every Zoho Bigin token refresh fails with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading error)', so Bigin calendar operations break for sync-enabled self-hosters — the new shared helper was wired into a caller whose axios-shaped contract it does not satisfy.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the token refresh now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and assigns its return to `tokenInfo` (previously always an Axios response). But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Immediately after, the code does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`, which assumes an Axios-shaped `{ data: ... }` object. A `Response` has no `data` property, so in sync mode this will throw (e.g., `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`) and break Zoho Bigin refresh behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode zohoCrmTokenInfo is a raw fetch Response, but the code evaluates zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error at line 217. With sync enabled, every Zoho CRM token refresh throws TypeError reading 'error' of undefined, so Zoho CRM-backed bookings fail for sync-enabled deployments; the refreshOAuthTokens return contract was never normalized for axios-based callers.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`) without JSON parsing/normalization. In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed token call was changed to `const zohoCrmTokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(async () => await axios(...), "zohocrm", credential.userId);` and the code immediately accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. If sync mode is enabled, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` will be a `Response` (no `.data`), so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and reading `.error` will throw, breaking token refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode resp is the parent app's response whose documented contract is {access_token, expiry}, but line 82 passes it to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's {code: 0, msg, data} envelope and treats any other body as an error. With sync enabled, every Lark token refresh is rejected by handleLarkError (code is undefined), so Lark Calendar fails for sync-enabled self-hosters even when the parent app returned valid tokens per the contract the PR itself documents.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call is wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then its result `resp` is passed to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`.
