adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] This new code unconditionally POSTs to Salesforce's token endpoint and writes the credential row on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, with no expiry check — previously jsforce refreshed lazily only when an API call hit an expired token. Every salesforce-connected booking and calendar operation now adds a Salesforce OAuth round-trip plus a credential UPDATE per operation, multiplying external API usage toward Salesforce rate limits, and any transient Salesforce error rejects the connection promise where previously valid cached tokens served the request.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new logic performs a refresh-token POST to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection` (see the added `fetch(...)` + `await prisma.credential.update(...)` block). There is no expiry/need check gating this refresh, so every time this code path runs it will add an external OAuth round-trip and DB write, and transient Salesforce errors now fail early via `throw new HttpError(...)`. This is a concrete perf/reliability/regression concern grounded in the diff, though not a strictly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED plus CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is one global switch that repoints the refresh parsing and traffic of all ~12 OAuth apps at once, with no per-app registry or opt-out. A self-hoster whose parent app implements only some integrations silently breaks refresh for every other app — the parent errors on unknown slugs while the minimum schema strips the fields — and no configuration shape can express partial support.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a global toggle `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (packages/lib/constants.ts) and then conditionally reroutes OAuth token refresh behavior for multiple apps through a single endpoint when `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Likewise, refresh-token parsing switches globally to a permissive `minimumTokenResponseSchema` under the same condition (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts), bypassing per-app schemas. There is no per-app enable/disable or registry in the diff; all updated integrations that call these helpers (google, office365, zoom, etc.) will be affected together once the env vars are set. The finding’s concern about inability to express partial support is thus diff-grounded, though claims about specific parent-app failure modes are not directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook JSON.parses the decrypted payload and writes it into credential.key without validating it against the target app's credential schema (googleCredentialSchema and its siblings). A parent sending a malformed or schema-drifted payload receives a 200 OK and bricks that user's integration — the app's own zod parse then fails on every operation, with nothing to distinguish a bad sync payload from a genuine auth failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts and `JSON.parse`s `reqBody.keys` and then writes it directly to `prisma.credential.update/create({ data: { key: keys } })` with no validation against an app-specific credential zod schema. The only validation performed is on the outer webhook body via `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema`; the decrypted `keys` payload is not schema-checked at all. This means a syntactically-valid but schema-invalid payload can be persisted and later cause runtime failures when app code expects a particular credential shape.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The outbound refresh request carries no authentication — no secret header of any kind — while the inbound webhook it pairs with requires one. Parent implementations cannot verify that a refresh request came from their Cal.com instance and must expose an unauthenticated endpoint that returns live access tokens for arbitrary (calcomUserId, appSlug) pairs to anyone who can reach it, or invent auth this client cannot send.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, the code `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` sends no authentication material (no shared secret header, no token, no signature). By contrast, the newly added inbound webhook endpoint `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` explicitly requires a secret header (`req.headers[CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME] === CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). The diff therefore provides no built-in way for the external "credential sync endpoint" to verify requests originated from this Cal.com instance, making the finding's security concern directly grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update path writes fresh keys without resetting the credential's invalid flag. A user whose credential was marked invalid by a failed auth receives synced fresh credentials but the row stays invalid, so reconnect-prompting flows keep treating the integration as broken and the synced keys are never used.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the update path only updates `key: keys`, but the diff does not show any `invalid`/`isInvalid` field on the `credential` model nor any logic that marks/reads such a flag. Because the existence and semantics of an “invalid flag” are not verifiable from this PR diff alone, the claim that the row will “stay invalid” and block flows cannot be confirmed from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full SafeParseReturnType envelope instead of the parsed data, forcing every caller to re-derive .success/.data and making the envelope-stored-as-credential bug representable (it already happened in googlecalendar). Returning data directly and throwing on failure deletes the success re-checks at the office365, zoom, and salesforce call sites and makes storing the envelope unrepresentable; the current contract invites the next caller to repeat the google bug.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function throws on parse failure but then returns the *entire* `SafeParseReturnType` envelope (`{ success: true, data: ... }`). This contract is then misused in at least one diff-grounded caller: `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` and stores it directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would persist the envelope instead of the credential data. Other call sites (office365/zoom/salesforce) also treat the return value as a safe-parse result (`.success/.data`), which is redundant given the internal throw and reinforces the confusing/bug-prone contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The office365 refresh path no longer logs the zod error and raw provider response that the removed console.error captured; failures now surface only as the detail-free 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. When Microsoft (or any provider) changes its token response shape, operators get a bare generic error with no field-level detail across every parseRefreshTokenResponse consumer, turning what was a five-minute diagnosis into blind debugging.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Office365-specific logging of Zod parse failures and the raw provider response. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", tokenResponse.error, "MS response:", responseJson)` block was deleted when switching from `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` to `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. The new shared helper `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` on parse failure, without including Zod error details or the response payload, so failures now surface as a generic message unless callers add their own logging. This is a real observability/debuggability regression grounded in the diff, not a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The appSlug contract is nine untypechecked string literals scattered across the call sites, each silently required to equal the app's slug in the App table and appStoreMetadata. Nothing validates the literals at compile time or runtime — this very diff already ships one wrong slug ('msteams' for office365video) — so parents silently receive slugs they cannot resolve; a typed constant or appStoreMetadata-keyed lookup would have caught it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce multiple hard-coded `appSlug` string literals passed into the new `refreshOAuthTokens(..., appSlug, userId)` helper across integrations (e.g. "google-calendar", "hubspot", "lark-calendar", "office365-calendar", "msteams", "webex", "zoho-bigin", "zohocrm", "zoomvideo"). There is no compile-time linkage to `appStoreMetadata` keys nor runtime validation that these literals correspond to the App table slug / `appStoreMetadata` slug, so a mismatch would silently break credential sync semantics. However, the specific claim that "msteams" is definitively wrong for `office365video` cannot be verified from this diff alone because the authoritative slug mapping (e.g., `appStoreMetadata` entry / app config) is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the full Zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) but this call site stores that envelope directly as the credential key (data: { key }), replacing the parsed credential value. Every Google Calendar token refresh — in the default non-sync configuration too — overwrites credential.key with {success:true,data:{...}}, so the next load reads credential.key.access_token/refresh_token as undefined and all Google calendar operations fail until the user re-authenticates.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`refreshTokenResponse`), i.e. the envelope `{ success, data, error }`, not the parsed credential payload (`.data`). However in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the result is assigned to `key` and persisted directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This will store `{success:true,data:{...}}` as `credential.key` instead of the expected credential shape. This happens regardless of sync being enabled because the non-sync branch also uses `schema.safeParse(response)` and still returns the envelope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys [z.string().toString()] evaluate to the single literal property name "[object Object]" (ZodString has no toString override), so the schema enforces only access_token and z.object strips every other property — the stated intent in the adjacent comments ("any property with a number is the expiry", "allow other properties") is not implemented at all. In sync mode every parsed token contains only access_token: office365/msteams/zoom persist stale expiry fields and re-refresh (sync-endpoint call plus credential DB write) on every calendar operation, and Salesforce's stored key loses instance_url/id so the next service construction connects with an undefined instance URL and its API calls fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`. `z.string()` returns a ZodString object and `.toString()` does not produce a dynamic key matcher; it will evaluate to a single literal key (effectively `"[object Object]"`), and Zod objects strip unknown keys by default. So in sync mode the parsed token data will typically retain only `access_token` (and possibly that one bogus key), dropping real fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`, `instance_url`, etc. This is diff-verifiable and can cause stale expiry persistence (e.g., Office365/Zoom using `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`) and data loss for Salesforce where the updated credential key is constructed from `accessTokenParsed.data`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync branch returns the credential-sync endpoint's raw fetch Response in place of each caller's direct-call response shape: google reads res?.data (undefined → TypeError), zoho-bigin/zohocrm read tokenInfo.data.error (undefined → TypeError), hubspot treats the Response as a HubspotToken, and lark feeds it to handleLarkError which rejects any non-Lark {code,msg,data} envelope. The credential-sync happy path — the feature this PR exists to deliver — crashes or corrupts credentials on the first refresh for google-calendar, hubspot, zoho-bigin, zohocrm and lark-calendar, so no self-hoster can actually run the sync flow end to end.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync branch does `return response;` where `response` is a `fetch()` `Response`. Multiple callers still assume the *original* non-sync return shapes: Google expects an axios-like `{ res: { data } }` and does `const token = res?.data;` then `token.access_token` (will be `undefined` when `res` is a `Response`), Hubspot assigns the result to `HubspotToken`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM treat the result as an axios response and read `.data.error`. These are verifiable mismatches introduced by the diff and would break the credential-sync path at runtime when enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] refreshOAuthTokens' sync-mode return (a fetch Response) is assigned to a HubspotToken and the unchanged downstream code reads expires_in/access_token on it, which a Response does not have. In sync mode expires_in is undefined so expiry_date becomes NaN (serialized as null) and the credential update spreads the Response — which has no own enumerable properties — wiping access_token and refresh_token from the stored key; the HubSpot integration dies silently on the next API call with no error at write time.

adjudication.rationale: In the new helper `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts), when sync mode is enabled it returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a Fetch `Response` object. In HubSpot’s CalendarService, the result is typed/treated as a `HubspotToken` (`const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`), and the existing downstream logic (immediately after the shown diff) relies on token fields like `expires_in`/`access_token` to compute expiry and persist updated credentials. A Fetch `Response` does not have those token fields, so in sync mode the refresh flow will break (token fields will be undefined), leading to incorrect expiry/credential updates. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff’s change to route refreshes through `refreshOAuthTokens` without parsing the sync-mode fetch response body into a token object.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This block performs an eager token refresh plus prisma.credential.update on every service construction and is the only integration rewiring in the PR not gated behind APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED/CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, silently rewriting default behavior that the PR's stated objective confined to opt-in self-hosters. Every existing Salesforce user now pays a blocking login.salesforce.com round-trip and a credential DB write per calendar operation, and any Salesforce throttle/5xx/network hiccup — checked via the fragile response.statusText !== "OK", which also discards the error body — fails bookings that previously succeeded using the still-valid stored token.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal string "refresh_token" into the parsed data whenever the field is absent — which is every sync-mode parse by construction, since minimumTokenResponseSchema strips it — and every caller persists that data. Sync-mode refreshes overwrite the parent-pushed real refresh token in stored credential keys with a junk sentinel; if the operator later unsets CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT to recover from a sync-endpoint outage, every synced credential fails refresh with invalid_grant and all affected users must re-authenticate.

adjudication.rationale: In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` parses with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not require `refresh_token`, and then forcibly sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when absent (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). At least one caller persists/propagates that injected value in a way that overwrites the real stored refresh token: Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the existing credentials (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };`) and then writes it to Prisma (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), so a missing `refresh_token` from the sync endpoint will replace the real refresh token with the literal sentinel. If sync mode is later disabled, refresh flows will use the now-corrupted refresh token and fail. This is a concrete, diff-introduced correctness/data-loss issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the credential row id) as the userId parameter of refreshOAuthTokens, while the eight other call sites in this diff all pass credential.userId. When credential sync is enabled the parent endpoint receives calcomUserId set to the credential's DB id, resolves the wrong or nonexistent user, and the zoho-bigin refresh fails or syncs tokens against the wrong identity.
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: refreshOAuthTokens is being called with credentialId instead of credential.userId/userId, causing incorrect user resolution and resulting in failed or misattributed credential/token sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler uses zod's throwing parse on req.body (and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) at lines 57-59) with no surrounding error handling, so malformed input produces an unhandled 500 rather than the 4xx contract the rest of the handler (403/404 paths) promises. A parent app sending a wrong-shaped body or keys encrypted with a mismatched key (e.g. mid-rotation) gets a raw 500 with no actionable message and cannot distinguish its own bad request from a server fault; a GET probe also 500s because req.body is undefined.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` handler, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called without any try/catch. If `req.body` is missing/undefined (e.g., a GET request, since the handler does not check `req.method`) or has the wrong shape, `parse()` will throw and Next.js will return a 500. Likewise, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))` can throw if decryption yields non-JSON (e.g., wrong/rotated key) or if the env key is empty, again producing an unhandled 500 rather than a controlled 4xx like the other branches (403/404) suggest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The O365 refresh failure mode was changed from log-and-continue (keep serving with the cached token when the refresh response failed schema validation) to a hard throw inside parseRefreshTokenResponse, without the feature-flag gating that scopes the rest of the sync changes. Any Microsoft token-response shape drift that zod rejects now fails every Office365 booking outright instead of proceeding with the still-valid cached access token, biting all O365 users rather than only sync-enabled self-hosters.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change Office365 refresh-token handling from non-fatal logging to a hard throw on schema validation failure. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(...)` plus `console.error(...)` was replaced with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, a failed `safeParse` results in `throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` regardless of `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (the flag only selects which schema to validate against). This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change with broader impact than the sync feature, but whether it is a "defect" vs an intentional tightening is not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook persists symmetricDecrypt's parsed output to credential.key without validating it against the target app's credential schema — the same schemas enforced at OAuth-callback time. A parent pushing a wrong-shaped key payload (missing or renamed fields) receives 200 "Credentials updated", and the corruption only surfaces later as per-booking failures with no error trail pointing at the push, leaving the operator debugging the wrong layer.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then written directly to `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` / `prisma.credential.create({ data: { key: keys, ... } })` with no schema validation for the target app. The only checks are user/app existence and `appStoreMetadata` lookup; nothing enforces that `keys` matches the credential shape expected by that app, so a wrong-shaped payload can be persisted while still returning 200 ("Credentials updated/created"). This matches the finding’s concern about silent corruption surfacing later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No test in the diff touches any of the new behavior — the webhook handler (auth rejection, decrypt, update-vs-create branches), refreshOAuthTokens' flag routing, or parseRefreshTokenResponse's two modes. Credential-key regressions ship silently to production; the envelope-wrapping corruption introduced in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts by this very diff is exactly the failure class a single store-then-reload round-trip test would have caught.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a concrete correctness defect in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: it replaces `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`, but `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a Zod `safeParse` result object (with `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential payload. The subsequent `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })` would therefore persist the wrapper object instead of the credential keys ("envelope-wrapping corruption"), breaking future reads/uses of the credential. While the finding also mentions missing tests, the bug is directly verifiable from the new helper's return value and its usage here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The credential-sync request carries no authentication material at all — no Authorization header, no CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET, no signature — so the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT must serve OAuth access tokens to any unauthenticated caller. Anyone who can reach the sync endpoint (internet-exposed deployment or a lateral network position) POSTs {calcomUserId, appSlug} and receives live OAuth access tokens for arbitrary cal.com users, yielding full access to their Google/Microsoft/Zoom/HubSpot integrations; the client offers no mechanism to attach credentials even if the operator's parent app wanted to require them, so every conformant implementation of this protocol is an unauthenticated token oracle.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, Cal.com POSTs to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body and does not attach any authentication material (no Authorization header, no shared secret, no signature). The diff also introduces `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`/header validation only for the inbound webhook (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), not for this outbound credential-sync token refresh call. As written, an operator implementing the sync endpoint has no application-layer way to verify the caller is Cal.com, making the protocol insecure-by-default and potentially turning the sync endpoint into an unauthenticated token oracle if it is reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The credential-write webhook authenticates with a single static shared secret sent verbatim in a header and binds nothing — no HMAC over the body, no timestamp, no nonce, no expiry — so possession of the one global secret authorizes replayable writes to every user's credentials. Any party that captures a single valid request (proxy/load-balancer logs, the parent app's outbound logs, a pasted curl) or the secret itself can forge or replay credential writes for any userId and any app indefinitely, silently replacing OAuth tokens that cal.com then uses for calendar and video operations; there is no freshness, no per-user scoping, and no replay detection, so secret rotation is the only remedy.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the only auth check is a direct equality comparison between a request header (`req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`) and a single global secret (`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). The handler then accepts arbitrary `userId` and `appSlug` from the body and writes credentials for that user/app (update/create via Prisma) with no per-user scoping, no request signing (HMAC over body), no timestamp/nonce, and no replay protection. This makes credential writes replayable/forgeable by anyone who learns the shared secret or captures one authorized request, matching the finding’s security concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook-secret check uses !==, a non-constant-time string comparison that leaks prefix-match timing on the sole authentication gate for arbitrary credential writes. An attacker with network access to the webhook can attempt byte-by-byte timing recovery of CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET (the endpoint adds no rate limit and V8 string comparison short-circuits at the first differing character), after which the full arbitrary-user credential-write access above applies; a crypto.timingSafeEqual comparison is the one-line fix.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the authentication gate compares the provided header value to `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` using `!==` (`req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). This is a normal string/byte comparison, not a constant-time comparison, and it’s the only protection before allowing arbitrary credential update/create for any `userId` in the request body. Using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (with proper Buffer normalization) would avoid the timing side-channel risk described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' (the second silently overwriting the first), so the schema enforces nothing beyond access_token: string, and this minimum schema is swapped in on global env flags — including for salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts whose refresh never routes through the sync endpoint, discarding its salesforceTokenSchema entirely. A self-hoster who enables credential sync gets every Salesforce token refresh persisted as {access_token, refresh_token} because the zod strip mode drops instance_url, signature, id, issued_at, scope, and expiry_date from the stored credential key (the same stripping drops expiry fields for Google/Zoom), corrupting the data jsforce and the expiry checks depend on, while sync-endpoint responses of any shape are persisted to user credentials with only access_token validated.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These are evaluated at definition time into *literal* property names (very likely both the same string, e.g. `"[object Object]"`, with the latter overwriting the former), so this does not create an index-signature/catchall and effectively validates only `{ access_token: string }` (plus at most one odd optional literal key). `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` switches to this minimum schema whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, regardless of whether the specific integration uses the sync endpoint. Multiple integrations now call `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` (e.g. `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), so when the flag is enabled the returned `.data` will be stripped down to (at best) `access_token` and then `refresh_token` may be replaced with the placeholder string (`"refresh_token"`) because the minimum schema strips it and the helper re-adds it. That is data loss/corruption of stored credential keys introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole Zod safeParse envelope ({success, data}) rather than the parsed data, and GoogleCalendarService persists that envelope directly as the credential key via data: { key }. On the first token refresh, prisma stores {success:true, data:{...}} as credential.key; every subsequent load runs googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key), which throws a ZodError because access_token/refresh_token are now nested under data, so all Google Calendar operations for that user fail until they re-authorize — this hits default deployments with no feature flag involved.

adjudication.rationale: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (i.e. `{ success, data, ... }`) rather than the parsed payload (`data`). In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned value is assigned to `key` and persisted via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, meaning the DB will store the envelope instead of the credential shape. This is verifiable from the diff: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` ends with `return refreshTokenResponse;` and never unwraps `.data`. The bug is not gated by `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`; even in the non-sharing path it uses `schema.safeParse(...)` and still returns the envelope.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When parsed data lacks refresh_token the function writes the literal string "refresh_token" into it, and under the credential-sharing branch the minimum schema strips refresh_token from every response, so the literal always fires. Office365CalendarService spreads tokenResponse.data over the existing credentials before prisma.credential.update (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264), so the first sharing-mode refresh overwrites the user's real Microsoft refresh token with the string "refresh_token" and persists it; the next refresh sends that garbage to Microsoft, fails, and the integration is dead until re-authorization. Same corruption hits Zoom's persisted newKeys spread.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, when credential sharing is enabled it validates with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, which does not include `refresh_token` and (as a plain `z.object(...)` without `.passthrough()`) will strip unknown keys from the parsed result. No `.json()` parsing occurs in the HubSpot code, so any subsequent access like `hubspotRefreshToken.expires_in` / `hubspotRefreshToken.access_token` would be `undefined` (because it's a `Response`, not token JSON), leading to incorrect expiry math and failure to persist updated credentials. This mismatch is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] On the sync path `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is a raw fetch Response, and the next statement reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`. `undefined.error` throws a TypeError on every Zoho CRM token refresh in sync-enabled deployments, failing all Zoho CRM calendar operations.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `zohoCrmTokenInfo` is now assigned from `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When sync is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) returns the result of `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)`, i.e. a raw `Response` object, not an Axios response. The next code still does `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`, but a `Response` has no `.data`, so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `.error` will throw a `TypeError` on the sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync endpoint is documented to return only access_token and expiry, but the Lark refresh passes that response to handleLarkError, which requires Lark's {code, msg} envelope. The envelope check fails on every refresh, so Lark token refresh always throws in sync-enabled deployments and Lark calendars stop working, surfacing as a misleading Lark API error rather than a sync-response-shape problem.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call is now wrapped with `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "lark-calendar", credential.userId)` and the returned `resp` is unconditionally passed into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`) documents that the sync endpoint response "should only contain the access token and expiry date" and it returns the raw `fetch` `Response` from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, not a Lark API response. This creates a shape/contract mismatch: in sync-enabled mode Lark’s refresh path still applies Lark-specific response handling to a non-Lark response, so refresh can break in credential-sync deployments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The SalesforceCalendarService constructor now unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com and rewrites the credential row on every service instantiation, with no expiry check and no timeout on the fetch. Every Salesforce event create/update/delete incurs a synchronous token refresh plus a DB write (inviting Salesforce token-endpoint rate limiting), and a slow or hung login.salesforce.com stalls those operations for the fetch duration — previously the constructor only built the Connection from stored tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an OAuth refresh unconditionally on instantiation: it `await fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before creating the `jsforce.Connection`. There is no expiry/"needs refresh" check shown and no fetch timeout/abort handling, so instantiation can add latency and risks rate-limiting/slow-hang behavior. However, the claim that *every* Salesforce event create/update/delete incurs this is not directly verifiable from this diff alone (depends on how often the service is constructed), so this is best classified as a concrete performance/architecture concern rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Refresh success is detected by comparing `response.statusText` to the string "OK" rather than `response.ok`, and the thrown HttpError's message is just the reason phrase. Any intermediary that normalizes or strips HTTP reason phrases turns every successful refresh into a thrown HttpError 400, and when a refresh genuinely fails the operator sees only "Bad Request"/"Unauthorized" with Salesforce's actual error body (e.g. invalid_grant) discarded — nothing to debug with.
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags the same core bug: determining OAuth refresh success by comparing `response.statusText` (e.g., to "OK") instead of using `response.ok`, which can misclassify successful responses and trigger failures (leading to bad/stale credential handling). It also adds extra related concerns about lost error details, but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The webhook's findFirst-then-create sequence has no unique constraint, upsert, or in-flight guard across the two awaits. Two overlapping syncs for the same user+app (a sender retry after a slow response is enough) both observe no credential and both create, leaving duplicate credential rows; later syncs update only one row while calendar selection can pick the stale duplicate, producing 401s that look like sync failures but are a split-brain credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` and then, in a later await, either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. This check-then-act sequence is not atomic and is vulnerable to concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` both seeing no row and both executing `create`, producing duplicates if the DB allows it, or throwing a unique-constraint error if such a constraint exists. The diff shows no transaction/upsert/in-flight guard around these two awaits, so the race is a real correctness issue introduced by this new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The decrypted `keys` object is persisted directly as the credential key with no validation against the target app's credential schema (or even a check that it is a non-empty object). A sender-side payload bug (wrong shape, wrong app's keys, empty object) is stored with a 200 "Credentials updated", silently overwriting the user's working credential; the corruption surfaces only later as failed bookings with no error at sync time.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the decrypted payload is accepted as `const keys = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and then persisted directly to `credential.key` via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` / `create({ key: keys, ... })` with no validation that `keys` matches the target app’s expected credential schema (or even that it’s a non-empty object). The only checks are that `user` exists, `app` exists, and `appMetadata` exists; `appMetadata.type`/`slug` are used but not to validate `keys`. Therefore a malformed-but-decryptable payload (wrong shape / empty object / wrong app’s keys) can overwrite an existing working credential while still returning 200 (“Credentials updated/created”), causing later failures.
